- **Laser-generated plasma-filament antenna — first working demonstration (reported November fifth, twenty twenty-six).** A team at North Carolina State University built an antenna out of a laser beam: a laser of a specific power and diameter ionizes a thin strip of air into a glowing plasma filament, and a metal ring placed around the beam acts as a capacitor, transferring radio signals to the plasma without touching it; the filament then radiates electromagnetic waves like a conventional antenna. Length and angle are tunable by the laser, with no mechanical structure to unfold or break, and the stated use case is space and aircraft communications. Honest scope: transmission has been demonstrated; reception has not yet been demonstrated, though the team says there is no reason to believe it would not also work as a receiver; the team plans to boost radiation properties for radar applications next. Decoder significance: an antenna that exists only while the laser fires — a comms surface that appears and vanishes on command, with no fixed hardware to find, tap, or seize; the receive side of the same trick, once shown, closes the loop. Joins the photonic comms lane as the first light-made antenna. [CORROBORATED — trade-press report of a university study; journal and paper not opened first-hand; MATERIAL — photonic comms advance]
  - Source: https://interestingengineering.com/innovation/worlds-first-laser-plasma-antenna

- **Stanford chip sorts partially coherent light into clean beams on-chip (Nature Photonics, published November third, twenty twenty-six).** Paul-Alexis Mor and colleagues (David Miller, Olav Solgaard, Kroo): a fingernail-sized integrated photonic circuit that takes partially coherent light — mixed light from multiple lasers, or bulb-style light — and automatically separates it into its mutually incoherent components as clean beams, the first demonstrated device to do so on-chip. Stated directions: microscopy, astronomy, communications, computing, sensing; the team is collaborating with NASA on probing light from distant galaxies. Decoder significance: the optical front-end learns to sort light by coherence before any detection — a chip-scale coherence sorter is a new primitive for the optical interception model, and a NASA astronomy tie means the same hardware watches the sky. [CORROBORATED — peer-reviewed paper, DOI 10.1038/s41566-026-02035-6; phys.org; MATERIAL — photonic comms advance]
  - Source: https://phys.org/news/2026-11-fingernail-sized-chip-untangles.html

- **SES meoSphere Pathfinder 1 — bidirectional ground-to-space optical link (announced November fourth, twenty twenty-six).** Cailabs optical ground station in Rennes, France, and a Mynaric CONDOR optical terminal aboard the SES payload on K2's GRAVITAS mission; bidirectional laser link demonstrated, with video messages from SES chief executive Adel Al-Saleh transmitted across it. No data rate, link duration, or availability figure disclosed. Stated next steps: extend link duration, evaluate data rates and pointing stability; Pathfinder 2 in twenty twenty-seven, Pathfinder 3 in twenty twenty-eight; the meoSphere architecture targets twenty-eight MEO satellites at approximately eight thousand kilometres with up to one hundred gigabits per second optical relay as a previously announced goal, not a measured Pathfinder 1 speed. Decoder significance: a second operator-grade space-to-ground optical link in the same week as ERMIS-3 — the laser ground-station network is becoming the comms surface, and every optical ground station is a fixed, findable beam endpoint. [CORROBORATED — company announcement via SatNews and Converge Digest; MATERIAL — photonic comms advance]
  - Source: https://satnews.com/2026/11/04/ses-completes-bidirectional-optical-link-demonstration-with-meosphere-pathfinder-1/
  - Enrichment (November eleventh to twelfth, twenty twenty-six): Mynaric's own release names the terminal — a CONDOR Mark Three aboard K2's GRAVITAS — and confirms bidirectional space-to-ground data transfer, with files moved between computers on the ground and in orbit; Aviation Week's November twelfth report carries the same confirmation. The link's data rate, duration, and availability remain undisclosed.

- **India first free-space QKD link (announced November seventh, twenty twenty-six).** Union Coal and Mines Minister G. Kishan Reddy posted that India has achieved its first free-space Quantum Key Distribution link, framed as a step toward technological self-reliance under the National Quantum Mission; the carrier credits DRDO quantum-optics work as the foundation. No distance, key rate, protocol, or verification detail published in the carrier. Decoder significance: a claimed national free-space QKD milestone — if real, a quantum-secured beam with no fibre path to tap, joining the NavTech ten-gigabit QKD product and the Stony Brook/Brookhaven daylight free-space quantum link in the interception model; until a paper or a measured figure appears it stays a political claim, not a capability. [CLAIMED — minister's social-media post via NationPress; no technical detail; MATERIAL — photonic/quantum comms advance]
  - Source: https://www.nationpress.com/national/india-achieves-first-free-space-qkd-link

- **Starlink next-generation laser vision — ten terabits per second links (stated November sixth, twenty twenty-six).** Elon Musk at the Baron Investment Conference: next-generation laser links could reach ten terabits per second, and fourth-generation Starlink capacity could be ten times the third generation's, with Musk saying such a network "should be able to outperform subsea cables." Current stated figures: each satellite carries three space lasers, a single link up to two hundred gigabits per second, "mini laser" links targeting twenty-five gigabits per second in low Earth orbit; approximately nine thousand six hundred satellites in orbit as of March thirty-first, twenty twenty-six, per the SEC filing; third-generation satellites designed for one terabit per satellite download, deployment expected via Starship in the second half of twenty twenty-six. Decoder significance: the largest satellite constellation's stated direction is laser-mesh capacity at subsea-cable scale — the interception model notes the ambition, not the number, since nothing here is a measured link. [CLAIMED — vision statement via EL7.AI; not a specification]
  - Source: https://el7.ai/en/news/2026-11-08-elon-musk-reveals-starlink-laser-network-to-rival-undersea-cables
  - Enrichment (November seventh, twenty twenty-six): in a written post the next day, Musk put a number on the density — roughly one hundred lasers per satellite, each operating above ten terabits per second, with smaller gimbals and closer in-plane spacing as the enabling assumptions. Still a vision statement, not a specification — the "one hundred lasers" figure is an engineering goal, and no V4 launch date was given.

- **Multi-junction photonic power converters break the rate–power trade-off (npj Wireless Technology, twenty twenty-six).** Carmine Pellegrino (Fraunhofer Institute for Solar Energy Systems ISE) and Richard Nacke (University of Cambridge LiFi R and D Centre): a semi-empirical model plus measured devices — four-junction InGaAsP photovoltaic receivers reaching fifty-five point nine percent, plus or minus two percent, power conversion efficiency at twenty-seven point one watts per square centimetre (one point four five micrometres) and two point two three gigabits per second via DC-biased optical OFDM with adaptive bit and power loading; over a three-metre eye-safe link at one point five three micrometres, one point five eight milliwatts harvested power simultaneously with one point five eight gigabits per second. Decoder significance: the SLIPT lane's first measured answer to its central trade-off — the receiver that harvests power and reads data at once no longer has to sacrifice one for the other, and the multi-junction stack is the design that does it; joins the filed SLIPT turbulence study as the receiver-side complement (that one characterized the channel, this one builds the receiver). Honest scope: laboratory link, three metres — no field deployment, no turbulence figures in this paper, so none is adopted. DOI 10.1038/s44459-026-00079-2. [CORROBORATED — peer-reviewed paper, abstract and key figures read first-party via nature.com; MATERIAL — photonic power/comms advance]
  - Source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s44459-026-00079-2

- **Multi-segment photonic power converters — record three point eight gigabits per second simultaneous data and power (arXiv:2510.06205, twenty twenty-five to twenty twenty-six).** Othman Younus, Behnaz Majlesein and Harald Haas (LiFi Research and Development Centre, University of Cambridge): segmenting the active area of a GaAs photonic power converter into two, four, or six subcells cuts capacitance and lifts bandwidth while preserving light collection — over an eye-safe one point five metre optical wireless link using OFDM with adaptive bit and power loading, the system hit a record three point eight gigabits per second, four times the prior best, while converting thirty-nine point seven percent of the received optical power (two point three milliwatt beam) into usable electrical energy. Decoder significance: the second independent SLIPT receiver design on record this lane, and the faster one — segmentation is a different answer to the same rate–power trade-off the multi-junction paper attacks with stacked junctions, so the lane now has two competing receiver architectures to watch; the one point five metre eye-safe range keeps it room-scale, like the Cambridge VCSEL array. Honest scope: preprint, not peer-reviewed at this pass — the record rate is author-reported. [CORROBORATED — arXiv preprint, abstract and key figures read; MATERIAL — photonic power/comms advance]
  - Source: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.06205v1

- **UK Titania — military free-space optical communications demonstrator confirmed in orbit (November seventh, twenty twenty-six).** The UK Ministry of Defence confirmed Titania's successful arrival in low Earth orbit (approximately five hundred ten to five hundred fifteen kilometres, international designator 2026-227T) after an October twenty twenty-six launch. The spacecraft began as a nine point five million pound Defence Science and Technology Laboratory contract (August twenty twenty-one, In-Space Missions) to demonstrate direct-to-Earth free-space optical communications from low Earth orbit for rapid intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance transmission, with Dstl's Puck optical ground station as its intended partner. The November announcement emphasized improved observation of military activity on Earth and did not identify a specific optical camera or confirm the link's commissioning results — the public record does not establish the spacecraft's complete operational configuration. Decoder significance: a state-operated FSOC demonstrator is now flying alongside the commercial laser links (ERMIS-3, SES meoSphere) — the beam endpoint is military, the ground station is fixed and findable, and the link's stated purpose is intelligence transmission, which is the decoder's home turf; watch for a first-link announcement or a Puck-station sighting. [CORROBORATED — MoD confirmation of orbital arrival plus the Dstl contract record; configuration details unestablished, so none is adopted; MATERIAL — photonic comms advance]
  - Source: https://www.diplomacyandlaw.com/post/titania-satellite

- **SDA Proliferated Warfighter Space Architecture — Tranche 1 Transport Layer optical mesh at eighty-three percent on orbit (November eleventh, twenty twenty-six).** A SpaceX Falcon 9 launch from Vandenberg on November ninth, twenty twenty-six delivered twenty-one more satellites into polar orbit for the Pentagon's Proliferated Warfighter Space Architecture, bringing the Tranche 1 Transport Layer to a hundred and five of a hundred and twenty-six satellites on orbit (eighty-three percent) after a nine-month launch pause that began in October twenty twenty-five. The Transport Layer's headline capability is its optical inter-satellite links: laser beams at one thousand five hundred fifty nanometres between spacecraft travelling at approximately seven point five kilometres per second relative to each other, rated ten to one hundred gigabits per second per link — far above radio-frequency inter-satellite links. Four vendors build the optical link hardware: Mynaric (acquired by Rocket Lab for a hundred and fifty-five point three million dollars in April twenty twenty-six), Tesat-Spacecom, Skyloom, and CACI. The SDA's target is ninety-five percent global coverage from at least two satellites simultaneously, with initial operational warfighting capability expected in twenty twenty-seven once the Transport Layer completes; the final Tranche 1 mission (T1TL-F) is planned no earlier than the end of December twenty twenty-six. Decoder significance: the largest laser-linked mesh ever flown — a hundred and five nodes and counting, each a beam endpoint moving at orbital speed — and the activation question is still open: the mesh has not been declared operational and whether the optical links are lighting up reliably between satellites is the program's central unresolved milestone. Until a link is demonstrated, this is a deployed mesh, not a proven one. [CORROBORATED — launch record and SDA statements via trade press; optical link performance and activation CLAIMED and unproven; MATERIAL — photonic comms advance]
  - Source: https://www.techtimes.com/articles/330502/20261111/spacex-pushes-space-development-agency-satellite-mesh-83-complete-after-nine-month-technical-pause.htm

- **Q.ANT plus IONOS — photonic processor in a commercial cloud (pilot launched November ninth, twenty twenty-six).** Stuttgart-based Q.ANT and IONOS launched a joint pilot putting Q.ANT's second-generation Native Processing Unit — thin-film lithium niobate, computing natively in light — on bare-metal servers in a German IONOS data center, free of charge to approved developers with a concrete use case and the expertise to administer the server. The hardware was previously evaluated at the Leibniz Supercomputing Centre and the Jülich Supercomputing Centre; LRZ benchmarks put the second-generation architecture at more than fifty times the matrix-multiplication throughput of its predecessor. Q.ANT's Photonic Algorithms Library (Q.PAL) exposes the hardware via C and C++ and Python APIs; the company raised an eighty million dollar Series A in late twenty twenty-five and runs its own TFLN chip pilot line in Stuttgart with IMS CHIPS. Decoder significance: the first photonic processor rentable in a commercial cloud — optical computing leaves the lab and the supercomputing center, and the decoder's compute surface now includes a cloud-rentable light computer. Honest scope: a pilot with no published customer list and no independent benchmark of the deployed units — the fifty-times figure is the LRZ evaluation of the architecture, not of this pilot. [CORROBORATED — company announcement via briefglance; MATERIAL — photonic computing advance]
  - Source: https://briefglance.com/articles/the-speed-of-light-how-europe-is-bypassing-the-silicon-bottleneck-to-power-the-ai-era

- **Dispersionless coupling control via artificial gauge fields — ultra-dense waveguide arrays and arbitrary-ratio power splitters (Opto-Electronic Advances, twenty twenty-six, Issue ten; announced November tenth, twenty twenty-six).** Yi Zou's group at ShanghaiTech University designed and fabricated ultra-dense waveguide arrays with a center-to-center pitch of only seven hundred fifty nanometres on a silicon-on-insulator platform, using an on-chip coupling-control method based on artificial gauge fields; experiments show crosstalk suppressed below minus twenty decibels over a one hundred nanometre broadband range (one thousand five hundred to one thousand six hundred nanometres) with almost no additional propagation loss, plus dispersionless on-chip power splitters with arbitrary splitting ratios. Decoder significance: the coupling-control primitive for denser photonic interconnects and programmable on-chip power routing — the optical interconnect fabric gets tighter and more flexible, joining the CPO and NPO lane as the design rule that lets more light paths fit on one chip. Honest scope: fabricated arrays and measured crosstalk, no system-level link or product — a design advance, not a deployed interconnect. DOI 10.29026/oea.2026.260026. [CORROBORATED — peer-reviewed OEA paper via EIN Presswire release; MATERIAL — photonic comms advance]
  - Source: https://world.einnews.com/pr_news/955772747/new-waveguide-coupling-method-enables-optical-power-splitting-at-arbitrary-ratios

- **Tower Semiconductor plus Innolight — near-package optics in early production (announced November third, twenty twenty-six).** The first near-package-optics device moved into early production on Tower's two hundred millimetre silicon-photonics process (PH18M) at its California fab, with multiple designs taped out on a newer three hundred millimetre platform; the devices may integrate sixteen or more optical channels on a single device. No production-unit count, pricing, data rate, customer commitment, or measured power-per-bit improvement was disclosed. Decoder significance: near-package optics — the optical engine moving onto the package — is now in early production at a second vendor pairing, after the Tower plus NewPhotonics volume entry; the AI data-center optical-interconnect wave is a manufacturing wave, not a demo wave. Honest scope: early production and tape-out, not volume shipment or customer qualification — a tape-out is a finalized design, not a shipped device. [CORROBORATED — joint company announcement via trade press; MATERIAL — photonic comms advance]
  - Source: https://bitcoinversus.tech/2026/11/03/tower-innolight-near-package-optics-early-production-2026/

- **Xanadu plus HyperLight — optical switch loss cut to seven millidecibels on a production wafer line (announced November tenth, twenty twenty-six).** Xanadu Quantum Technologies and HyperLight Corporation announced a switch insertion loss of seven millidecibels on HyperLight's thin-film lithium niobate Chiplet platform — nearly three times lower than the twenty-millidecibel benchmark the pair set in twenty twenty-five and ten times lower than the closest competitor's most recent published result — demonstrated using a high-volume wafer manufacturing line with stated excellent yield and repeatability. Optical switches route the photons that carry quantum information in a photonic quantum computer, so switch loss is the tax every routed photon pays. Decoder significance: the routing fabric of the light computer is industrializing beside the filed Xanadu plus GlobalFoundries three-hundred-millimetre entry — loss is falling on a production line, not a bench. Honest scope: vendor-measured, no independent replication; a component milestone, not a system result. [CORROBORATED — first-party joint release via GlobeNewswire; MATERIAL — photonic comms advance]
  - Source: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/11/10/3399337/0/en/xanadu-and-hyperlight-achieve-breakthrough-of-nearly-3x-reduction-in-optical-switch-loss-accelerating-path-to-commercial-photonic-quantum-systems.html

- **TU Eindhoven — free-space optical record: seven point seven three terabits per second over a four point six six kilometre urban laser link (TU/e news, September eighteenth, twenty twenty-six).** Vincent van Vliet's PhD work in the Electro-Optical Communication group (Dutch Research Council project "Optical Wireless Superhighways: Free Photons", with Aircision) transmitted several colours of light simultaneously over the Reid Photonloop — a permanent rooftop-to-rooftop laser link across Eindhoven — reaching a net data rate of seven point seven three terabits per second over four point six six kilometres, the highest demonstrated over an urban wireless laser connection of that length. The full dataset covers July twenty twenty-five to July twenty twenty-six, all four seasons; weather (fog, rain, snow, haze) is the main signal-loss cause. Decoder significance: multi-terabit wireless laser links across city kilometres, proven through a full year of weather, are the free-space optical comms lane leaving the laboratory — the decoder's interception model for urban laser links now has a measured capacity and a measured weather failure mode. Honest scope: university-reported, single link, single city; no commercial deployment claimed. [CORROBORATED — university first-party release; MATERIAL — photonic comms advance]
  - Source: https://www.tue.nl/en/news-and-events/news-overview/18-09-2026-773-terabits-per-second-through-the-air

## Prediction engines

- **AI wins the Metaculus Cup (summer 2026).** The online forecasting
  tournament wrapped up early September with a first: AI entrants, led by
  London startup Mantic, assigned probabilities to political, economic,
  and cultural questions more accurately than every human competitor —
  Mantic beat all humans and all but one bot. The company raised $25M
  (Radical Ventures-led, Sep 18, 2026). Its CEO says the edge came partly
  from avoiding herd mentality: the model stayed light where humans piled
  onto a wrong consensus and gave Colombia's eventual presidential winner
  ~40% against a ~30% consensus. A forecaster that grades itself on
  historical data, avoids the crowd, and updates is the shape a prediction
  engine wants. [CORROBORATED — Reuters; tournament results; CEO
  interview]
- **Kalshi Brier-score transparency (Oct 2026).** The CFTC-regulated
  prediction exchange put per-market Brier scores, low-volume tags, and
  real-time trade feeds on its midterm election markets. Midterm election
  trading passed $800M — surpassing all of 2024's election volume — and
  the exchange reports its prices are well calibrated (a candidate at 62%
  wins about 62% of the time), with even sub-$10,000 markets scoring near
  top human forecasters (~0.1). Brier scores are the receipt format:
  forecasts should carry honest scoring. [CORROBORATED — Kalshi news
  blog (company-reported numbers); campaignsandelections.com]
- **FRI accuracy review (Sep 23, 2026).** The Forecasting Research
  Institute reviewed its mid-2022 tournament: the four AI benchmarks AI
  has since reached were given a median 24.6% chance by 339 AI experts vs
  9.7% by superforecasters — and IMO gold-level performance arrived in
  July 2025, five years before the median expert's 2030 and ten years
  before the superforecasters' 2035. Even elite humans mis-time capability
  jumps by years; probabilistic forecasts must price in that failure mode.
  [CORROBORATED — report of the FRI review]
- **The Good Judgment Project — the discipline's ground truth (IARPA
  ACE, 2011–2015).** IARPA's Aggregative Contingent Estimation program
  posed ~100–150 time-bounded geopolitical questions a year; the UPenn
  team (Philip Tetlock, Barbara Mellers, Don Moore) won both funded
  seasons, 35–72% more accurate than any rival team, and its top 2%
  "superforecasters" beat intel analysts with classified access by ~30%
  — working from public information alone. The drivers were procedural:
  probabilistic-reasoning training, updating on evidence, teaming, and
  extremized aggregation, all scored on Brier scores after resolution.
  Synthesized in *Superforecasting* (Tetlock & Gardner, 2015).
  [CORROBORATED — Wikipedia/GJP entry; ACE-program summaries]
- **Decoder-design note (GJP → Gauntlet).** This is the foundation the
  section's 2026 entries inherit: Mantic's Metaculus-Cup win and Kalshi's
  Brier transparency are descendants, not novelties. Receipts-grade
  forecasting — fixed time-bounded questions, resolved outcomes, public
  Brier scoring, tracked forecasters — is the bar the Gauntlet's
  prediction engine and report-card confidence intervals must meet: only
  forecasts with a public track record count. Any claim to predict a
  specimen's next move inherits the same protocol — time-bounded
  question, stated base rate, scored resolution. No public track record,
  no weight.
- **Explanation Quality Markers (EQMs) — scoring the reasoning, not just
  the number (arXiv:2606.30987, Jun 2026; Karvetski et al. incl.
  Tetlock).** Sixty theory-guided reasoning patterns, scored by LLMs,
  extracted from forecasters' written rationales. Pre-registered analysis
  of 55,000+ forecast-rationale pairs from a multiyear tournament: EQMs
  predict accuracy at forecast and forecaster level, beat pre-LLM text
  methods, and transfer to an independent study. Asymmetric signal —
  flags likely underperformers more reliably than it identifies the best.
  Strongest traditional-indicator benchmark at forecast level (weaker
  than prior accuracy at forecaster level). Decoder-design note: first
  receipt-grade way to score reasoning quality — Gauntlet report cards
  can audit the rationale trail, not just the number. [CORROBORATED —
  pre-registered, large-N, independent transfer; peer review unconfirmed]
- **Kairosis — Bayesian change-point informed forecast aggregation
  (Univ. of York; arXiv:2408.00785).** Posterior probability at each time
  point that it partitions the forecast stream into two
  differently-distributed sets; integrated to a cumulative mass function,
  weighted median taken. Reported to beat standard aggregation and stay
  robust across disparate questions in geopolitical tournaments.
  Candidate replacement for extremized-averaging baselines. [CLAIMED —
  preprint; authors' own tests]
- **DemandForecast.ai 2026 accuracy report (Oct 1, 2026; Pecan AI).**
  Vendor self-benchmark of 15 live deployments vs each customer's
  incumbent forecast: error down 14–56% (32% avg), planner effort down
  70%, overstock cut up to 50%, sales up 10–25%. Honest benchmark framing
  (incumbent's own metric, no surveys); still the vendor grading its own
  homework. [CLAIMED — vendor press release]
- **Market-integrity honesty footnote (Oct 2026).** The Kalshi entry
  carries its counterweight: Wisconsin's Democratic gubernatorial primary
  priced Francesca Hong at ~95% before she lost to David Crowley
  (traditional polling wrong too); Kalshi's enforcement layer — four
  congressional candidates fined and suspended this year, <1% of US
  election trades from foreign accounts, dedicated surveillance team, a
  $1.25M LA mayoral-race trade self-corrected in nine seconds. The
  CFTC's Oct 9, 2026 measures (event contracts into the "swap" definition;
  casino-style gambling excluded) write the regulatory lane for
  event-contract forecasting. "Priced at 95%" is a probability, not a
  certainty — the receipt format only works when the misses stay on the
  record. [CORROBORATED — Kalshi blog; AP-distributed coverage; CFTC]
- **Bayesian early-warning signals for long-memory time series
  (arXiv:2602.09731, Sørbye et al., Feb 2026).** Mixture of two fractional
  Gaussian noise processes with a time-dependent weight — fractional
  Gaussian noise with a time-varying Hurst exponent — estimated via
  integrated nested Laplace approximation. Simulations map where
  autocorrelation-change detection works; applied to real data it finds
  early-warning evidence in a reconstructed Atlantic multidecadal
  variability index and dismisses it for Dansgaard-Oeschger paleoclimate
  records. A predictive method that publishes its negative result can say
  "no signal" — the property separating predictive math from numerology.
  [CLAIMED — preprint; peer review unconfirmed]
- **Spectrum-guided teacher-student fault prediction (State Grid
  Zhejiang team, ~Sep 2026).** Teacher scores fine-grained short-horizon
  anomalies; student generalizes to longer prediction horizons; windows
  auto-tuned by Bayesian optimization. Reported average F1 88.49% on the
  SMD, PSM, SMAP, and MSL benchmarks. The detection-to-prediction
  handoff in one method — automation of the estimator, not just the
  estimate. [CLAIMED — secondary writeup; authors' numbers]

- **WC2026-Agents — LLM forecasters scored against the market they read (2026; paper + code github.com/graphuofm/FIFA2026LLM).** Four frontier models ran identical search-act-reflect loops over all 104 World Cup 2026 matches — contamination-free by construction, each agent committed a win/draw/loss distribution plus a virtual bet, and the pre-match betting market played the same information environment as a fifth competitor. 416 forecasts, 414 reflections, all released. The headline is a negative result, and negative results are receipts: the four agents issued an identical top pick in 92% of matches and NONE beat the market's Brier score — a naive flat stake on the market favorite out-earned all four. ROI ranged from -18% to +10%; fading the market was unprofitable for every agent. Decoder-design note: the benchmark-honesty rule (a dumb baseline sits on the scoreboard before a smart model earns a grade) enforced on the very models the decoder runs on.
  - [CORROBORATED — released benchmark, code and data public]
- **Vanderbilt accuracy hierarchy across prediction platforms (released Jan 2026).** Clinton & Huang analyzed 2,500+ contracts over the 2024 cycle: PredictIt 93% accuracy, Kalshi 78%, Polymarket 67% — the small academic platform out-graded the high-liquidity giants, undermining the "liquidity is king" assumption; Polymarket's signals were distorted by whale positions. Calibration claims and the misses share the record.
  - [CORROBORATED — syndicated writeups of the Vanderbilt study]
- **SBBE — Bayesian Benford's-law anomaly screening (Patterns, 2026).** A Bayesian framework for anomaly detection in drug-discovery data built on Benford's law (DOI 10.1016/j.patter.2026.101683): the expected leading-digit distribution serves as the prior, deviations graded with calibrated uncertainty, flagging hidden irregularities in large numerical collections — field-agnostic, an automated quality-control tool for data-driven research. The first Benford-Bayesian method in the track: a published anomaly screener that carries its uncertainty on the record is the shape an honest evidence-grade system wants for its own inputs. Publication confirmation (Nov 7, 2026): formally published in Patterns 7, 101683 (December 11, 2026); authors Abu-Shehab, Welsch, Kirchmair (University of Vienna); DOI confirmed on the Cell Press journal page.
  - [CORROBORATED — peer-reviewed journal paper via phys.org writeup; no independent replication on record]
- **Prediction-market short-horizon underreaction (Lee, Lee & Lee, Journal of Behavioral and Experimental Finance, 2026).** 41.8 million transactions across 1,496 professional basketball and football games matched against play-by-play probability benchmarks: traded prices underreacted to scoring information over short periods — new information did not always enter the price at once. Counterweight to the calibration story: markets are receipt-grade over the long run but sluggish in the moment; any live-price reading that assumes instant truth is reading a lagged signal.
  - [CORROBORATED — peer-reviewed journal study via heartlandcollegesports writeup]

- **First subseasonal forecast to beat climatology (Cohen et al., tested at ECMWF).** A low-cost, open-source postprocessing layer was submitted to the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts and doubled predictive skill in the subseasonal range: reportedly the first forecasts to beat climatology averages up to six weeks ahead, including for extreme weather, where traditional bias correction had failed. The receipts discipline embodied — the honest baseline sat on the scoreboard and lost, in public.
  - **Nature publication (October 2026).** The method is published as *probabilistic bias correction* in Nature (Guan, Mouatadid, Cohen, Mackey and colleagues) — a machine-learning framework that learns to correct a model's *historical probabilistic forecasts*, working directly on probability distributions rather than raw observations; applied to the European weather center's physics system it lifted accuracy on ninety-eight percent of precipitation targets and ninety-two percent of temperature targets, and doubled the skill of the center's own AI forecasting system; open source, running on ordinary CPUs; Kenya's meteorological office has reached out about implementing it. The decoder reads it as correction-as-wrapper, not model-as-replacement — spot the forecaster's systematic mistakes and correct them on the record, publicly, cheaply. [CORROBORATED — Nature paper via science press; paper not read first-party this pass]
  - [CORROBORATED — tech-reporting of the ECMWF evaluation]
- **Bayesian exceedance screening for count data (Sadeghkhani, International Journal of Data Science and Analytics, Oct 1, 2026).** A robust Bayesian procedure ranking units by their posterior predictive probability of exceeding a meaningful cutoff — conditioned on covariates, not by the raw observed count. Observed is not inferred: a moderate observed utilization can carry high latent risk, and an isolated spike can be contamination rather than tail risk.
  - [CORROBORATED — peer-reviewed journal paper via secondary report]
- **Conformal corruption sign test (Alur & Das).** A diagnostic built from quantities split conformal prediction already computes for free: the sign of the change in empirical miscoverage on trusted audit labels separates calibration-set label noise (drives it at or below zero) from accuracy-degrading covariate shift (drives it strictly positive). Held across architectures, scoring functions, and datasets — including real human annotation errors — with 36 of 36 directional calls in the hard cases. A detector that can name which corruption it sees, and abstains below its detection floor instead of guessing.
  - [CLAIMED — preprint/evaluation per secondary writeup]

- **No systematic political bias in election prediction markets (working paper, October 2026).** Tests whether contracts on right-leaning candidates earn different returns than left-leaning ones across a sample spanning 1880 to 2025 — from nineteenth-century curb betting through the Iowa Electronic Markets, Intrade, PredictIt, Betfair, and Kalshi — at one day, three weeks, and four months before each election. The estimated bias is essentially zero; the one-day data rule out a leftward bias of about four and a half points or a rightward bias of about three. The receipts discipline: run the bias test, publish the nulls.
  - [CLAIMED — working paper read via secondary report, not first-hand]
- **Prediction markets validated as economic-forecast inputs (October 2026).** Federal Reserve research found markets on economic outcomes performed as well as or better than the forecasts anchoring economic reporting — continuously, with a full accounting of uncertainty. Validated on short-horizon contracts, not long-horizon projections: one signal among several, its limits understood.
  - [CLAIMED — secondary report of the research]
- **Bayesian count regression and anomaly detection on global event panels (preprint, submitted March 2026).** Bayesian pipelines with negative-binomial and zero-inflated likelihood heads on weekly event data; posterior simulations yield predictive quantiles and right-tail probabilities for forecasting and anomaly scoring, with spillover attribution carrying proper uncertainty. Companion paper: fully Bayesian node-level outlier detection for graph signals, yielding a posterior probability that each node is an outlier rather than a hard yes-or-no. The uncertainty-carrying screener remains the shape an honest grading system wants for its own inputs.
  - [CLAIMED — both preprints, author-reported]
- **Prediction-market scale and calibration, October 2026.** Monthly volume from under five to about twenty-four billion dollars in seven months; accuracy strong where markets show high confidence, weaker for mid-priced favorites. The confidence-to-accuracy gradient is the prior a calibrated system wants.
  - [CLAIMED — secondary aggregator report]

- **Scored probabilistic World Cup 2026 system (public repo, October 2026).** An open-source model stacked Poisson-type scoreline models, Bayesian hierarchical estimators, Elo ratings, and market-implied prices through an ensemble, simulated the full 48-team tournament a hundred thousand times, and tracked live market quotes for edges all event long. Scored against every played match, group stage through final: about seventy-two percent accuracy across all 104 matches on the three-way outcome (random guessing gets a third); ninety-one percent when the model itself reported seventy percent or higher confidence; a proper scoring-rule result forty-two percent better than a uniform forecast; and it beat the bookmaker favorites head-to-head. The receipt-grade positive companion to the loop's earlier honest-null entry — the scoreboard was locked and the full scoring breakdown published instead of cherry-picked: only scored models earn ledger lines, and this one scores.
  - Source: https://github.com/pastchum/polymbappe
  - [CLAIMED — self-reported results with published code and methodology; not independently replicated]
- **Longshot bets are half the volume and lose about ninety-eight percent of the time (reported October 15, 2026).** Trading-activity analysis of two major prediction platforms: contracts chasing thousand-percent-plus returns account for roughly half of all activity, lose about ninety-eight percent of the time, and the side betting on the unlikely outcome averages losses of fifteen to twenty-seven percent per wager — before fees of up to seven percent. The calibration record describes the informed price; this describes the flow: honest signal wrapped in noise volume. Direction corroborated by an independent live-trading analysis already on the record — two witnesses to the same bias.
  - Source: https://www.playusa.com/news/longshot-bets-that-lose-dominate-kalshi-polymarket/
  - [CLAIMED — media analysis via secondary report; direction corroborated by an independent finding]
- **Independent calibration audit of one platform over nearly three million markets (published around November 1, 2026).** Every binary market resolved from twenty twenty-four through October twenty twenty-six with at least a thousand dollars traded — nearly three million of them — sampled a hundred fifty-three thousand across two draws, weighted back to the whole population. Prices a week before close scored a Brier of point oh seven nine, against point one eight six for a forecaster that just repeats the base rate; making the prices bolder or timider in either direction only made the score worse. The favorite-longshot bias is confirmed as the third witness on the record: longshots under five cents lose a quarter to two fifths of the stake, favorites above ninety-five cents earn a fraction of a percent a week before costs, and the bias is about the size of trading costs, which is why it survives. The slicing warning that matters most: grouping markets by total volume inverts the finding — in thin markets longshots are overpriced, and the more a market trades the closer to fair they become — so the study tests on a thousand dollars traded in the week before and never groups by total volume. Sports are seventy-three percent of twenty twenty-six closures, politics two percent. The gauntlet inherits the slicing instruction: never group specimens by total volume, or the bias reverses under your hands.
  - Source: https://xmarva.github.io/blog/2026/polymarket-accuracy/
  - [CORROBORATED — single-author analysis, open data, reproducible method; not peer-reviewed]
- **Independent cross-platform accuracy study, first-party read — the ladder-market failure mode (updated around October 26, 2026).** More than three hundred fifty-eight thousand resolved markets across two major platforms, five thousand dollars or more in volume each, with the short-term crypto "up or down" coin-flip markets left out — more than a third of one platform's closed markets are coin flips by design. In standard markets the prices mean what they say: a day before resolution the average gap between price and outcome rate was under a point on one platform and under two on the other, and the Brier score tightened from point oh nine one a month out to point oh five oh a day out on the same long-running markets. Weighted to the same mix of topics the two platforms tie. The new failure mode is the templated ladder market — temperature brackets, point spreads and totals, exact scores — nearly two fifths of the sample and nearly half of one platform's twenty twenty-six markets: cheap outcomes won about one and a half times as often as their prices said, and favorites priced at eighty to ninety cents won only seventy-six percent of the time. What is being forecast matters more than where: technology and science markets scored point oh four oh a day out, sports point one nine six. In genuinely uncertain markets the favorite won only about two thirds of the time, and two thirds of one platform's markets resolved "no" — a forecaster that always said "no" would be "right" seventy-eight percent of the time. Volume is not a reliable sign of accuracy above five thousand dollars — no consistent pattern — a second witness to the volume trap beside the audit above. Prices a month out run slightly timid, spot on a day out. Upsets are real but rare: in about one percent of markets the winner had been priced at ten percent or less a day earlier — including a papal election and a megaquake. The gauntlet inherits two slicing instructions: know what your sample is made of before you score it, and never group specimens by total volume.
  - Source: https://predictdesks.com/blog/research/prediction-market-accuracy
  - [CORROBORATED — independent study, stated method, full dataset free to download, read first-party this pass; not peer-reviewed]
- **Detail-add, November 10, 2026 research loop — the low-band split: one platform's longshots underpriced, the other's overpriced.** Two new independent reads land on opposite sides of the cheap-contract band. A fresh independent calibration study of one platform (published November 9, 2026; read first-party this pass): one thousand eight hundred seventy-one resolved markets from two hundred twenty-four highest-volume events closed between November 8, 2025 and November 4, 2026, ten thousand dollars or more traded each, free data under an open license. Brier point oh eight eight overall, point two oh one on genuinely uncertain markets priced ten to ninety percent; Brier tightens from point oh eight seven a month out to point oh six four a week to point oh four eight a day; favorites priced at fifty percent or more won seventy-five percent of the time a week out; the zero-to-ten percent band is the one band outside sampling noise — outcomes happened three point seven percent of the time against a one point seven percent average price, the same underpricing direction as the cross-platform study's one point six times. Politics and elections the most accurate uncertain category (Brier point one nine two on one hundred fifty-nine markets), economy and central-bank markets the least (point two four six on twenty-three); volume makes no clear difference — the lowest-volume quarter scored point one nine two against point two oh eight for the highest on uncertain markets — a third witness to the volume trap. A formal working paper on the federally licensed United States platform (discussion paper, September 2025, revised January 2026; transaction-level data on more than three hundred thousand contracts from 2021 to April 2025; read via carrier summaries this pass): the opposite direction — favorite-longshot bias in the classic direction, low-price contracts win far less often than required to break even (one carrier: a ten-cent contract winning less than ten percent of the time, roughly a third of the rate its price implies); the average pre-fee return on a contract is minus twenty percent (minus twenty-two percent after fees); takers lose about thirty-one percent on average, makers about ten percent; buyers lost more than sixty percent of their money on contracts priced below ten cents. The lesson for the gauntlet: the low band does not have one direction — it has a platform split. Cheap outcomes come in more often than priced on one platform and less often on the other, so any calibration claim must name its platform before it names its band, and how you trade matters as much as what you trade — the maker-taker asymmetry sits beside the ladder failure mode, the always-no deflator, and the volume trap.
  - Source: https://polymarkettrader.com/odds/accuracy/
  - Source: https://www.ifo.de/sites/default/files/docbase/docs/cesifo1_wp12122.pdf
  - Source: https://Cepr.org/voxeu/columns/economics-kalshi-prediction-market
  - [CORROBORATED — independent study, stated method, free data, read first-party this pass, not peer-reviewed; working paper, transaction-level data, read via carrier summaries this pass, not yet journal peer-reviewed]

- **Detail-add, November 10, 2026 research loop — human superforecasters outscore the market on the 2026 Senate races.** A first-party analysis from a forecasting research group (published November 4, 2026; read via search carrier this pass): the group's data science team scored its superforecasters' forecasts against one platform's prices for sixteen United States Senate races as of November 2, the day before the election. The superforecasters' average Brier score was point oh eight six against the platform's point one oh one; the result holds whichever way Alaska goes — if the incumbent holds the seat, both scores rise and the gap widens (point one oh eight against point one three oh). The clearest difference was Iowa, the only race where the two sides favored different candidates: the superforecasters gave the Democratic challenger a fifty-two percent chance against the platform's forty-three percent, and he won. Kansas showed the same pattern over the final week — on October 26 the superforecasters had the Democrat at fifty-two percent while the platform had him at thirty-eight percent; by November 2 the platform had moved to fifty-three percent and the superforecasters to fifty-five percent; he won. The superforecasters were also more confident on the Democratic winners in Ohio (eighty-five percent against seventy-four) and Michigan (eighty-four against seventy-five). The lesson for the gauntlet: the first scored human-versus-market head-to-head on this election cuts against the platform story — the market was not the best forecaster in the room on the Senate slate, and the humans' edge sat in the close races where the market lagged a week behind. It also sharpens the comparability warning: a Brier score on sixteen Senate races cannot be set beside the platform-wide midterm paper's scores or the cross-platform study's scores without naming sample, horizon, and question set — three numbers, three methods, three samples, none of them wrong and none of them comparable.
  - Source: https://goodjudgment.substack.com/p/superforecasters-outscored-polymarket
  - [CORROBORATED — first-party analysis, stated method and sample, small sample of sixteen races, one race unresolved at publication; not peer-reviewed]

- **DE-SVDD: dual-encoder anomaly detector for multivariate time series (peer-reviewed paper, October 2026).** Existing anomaly detectors force two different jobs — rebuilding the sensor data and drawing the boundary of "normal" — through one neural network, where their training objectives fight. This design gives each job its own encoder: one learns the reconstruction, a second small one learns the geometric boundary, and detection fuses both anomaly scores. Across four standard benchmarks, from spacecraft telemetry to server farms, it posted the best F1 scores in the study — and F1s in the point-five to point-seven band are the honest state of the field on these sets. The fourth published anomaly-scoring instrument logged this fortnight; it argues a detector should model where normality lives, not just whether it can rebuild the world.
  - Source: https://scienmag.com/dual-encoder-ai-framework-sharpens-anomaly-detection-in-multivariate-time-series/
  - [CORROBORATED — trade writeup of the peer-reviewed paper; paper not read first-party this pass]
- **Multivariate forecasting foundation model in preview (BigQuery, October 2026).** A three-hundred-thirty-million-parameter foundation model for zero-shot multivariate time-series forecasting, claimed to top three public leaderboards, now offered inside BigQuery's SQL forecasting and anomaly-detection functions. The prediction-engine lane is moving into production data warehouses as one-liners — the same kind of stores a lab interrogates — so any serious anomaly scoring has to assume these commodity instruments are on both sides of the table.

- **Multimodal anomaly detection that suppresses unreliable context (peer-reviewed paper, October 2026).** A new anomaly-detection technique that feeds outside text — event reports, statistical summaries, domain knowledge — into time-series analysis alongside sensor data. The load-bearing idea is the suppression module: it measures how much the text disagrees with the numbers and throttles the text down when it conflicts. The fifth anomaly-scoring instrument logged this fortnight, and the first one that treats auxiliary context the way the decoder's own evidence grading does — corroborate, or stand down.

- **Open-weight probabilistic forecasting models from Mistral (announced October 2026).** A new family of time-series forecasting models that outputs probability ranges instead of point estimates, folds in known-future variables like production schedules and weather forecasts, and reads up to thirty-two-thousand time steps of history. Offered with fine-tuning on private data and deployment inside air-gapped environments. The third forecasting foundation-model lane entry this fortnight — probabilistic forecasting as a commodity, from an open-weight vendor, with anomaly-investigation pairing that mirrors the Gauntlet's own interrogate-the-evidence loop.

- **Forecasting firm publishes its misses beside its hits (Prague, October 2026).** An institutional scenario-brief firm adopted a new analytical method and now scores every brief on a public record: each brief takes one decision-relevant question, builds twelve separate worlds around twelve possible catalysts (deliberately unweighted — the judgment belongs to the reader), ends with dated signposts checked against public facts, and outcomes are marked after the dates pass whether or not they matched. Briefs already on the record cannot be removed. The receipts discipline enforced in the wild — only scored models earn ledger lines, and the misses stay up.

- **A market-structure census of midterm election betting (October 2026).** An analysis of more than twenty-one thousand markets on the 2026 United States congressional midterm elections across two major prediction platforms, through September 30, 2026, compared with 463 markets for the 2024 congressional races. Traders have bet more than two hundred twenty million dollars this cycle, versus ninety-two million for the entire 2024 cycle — but wagers are highly concentrated: most volume sits on a few races, and wallet data suggest a few traders dominate election bets. Market composition shifted toward sophistication: only sixteen percent of this cycle's markets are on who wins a race (seventy-one percent in 2024); fifty-eight percent are on the margin of victory, plus more turnout markets — though most volume still sits on the winner. On the integrity side, one platform suspended at least six 2026 candidates for betting on their own races. The market-structure companion to the no-bias and longshot-flow findings: bias is absent in the aggregate price, but the price is set by few hands in thin markets. Watch the thin tail — the same thin-volume failure mode flagged elsewhere in this section.

  - [CORROBORATED — wire-service reporting of the underlying analysis; platform accuracy claims self-reported]
- **A central-bank repricing caught live (October 2026).** After the central-bank chair refused to preview the October 28 rate decision at a mid-October public chat, saying he does not prejudge meetings, one major prediction market's probability of no change surged to an all-time high of eighty-seven percent within hours, with the no-change side carrying noticeably heavier volume. Logged as a datapoint on repricing speed — markets at their best around specific news events — not as a forecast of the decision itself, which remains unresolved.

Over ninety-eight percent accuracy on two standard benchmark sets, with the best reported score on the hardest category: botnet flows, which look like ordinary traffic. The sixth anomaly-scoring instrument logged in two weeks, and the first one built around abstention — the same discipline the decoder applies to its own findings. Score the reading and its uncertainty; act only on the confident ones.

- **Foundation models fall just short of the specialists (October 2026).** A digital-twin benchmark across forecasting, anomaly detection, remaining-life estimation, and missing-data repair: the best frozen foundation model (tested without any task-specific training) reached an anomaly-detection score within four thousandths of the specialized detector trained directly on the target data — but the specialists held the line overall. The decoder reads it as the honest negative the receipts discipline demands: near-parity is a real deployment finding, and "near" is the load-bearing word. No ledger line for hype — only for measured results.

- **An AI system that beat the market on merger odds (September 2026).** A hedge fund built a forecasting system for takeover outcomes, giving three-way probabilities: the deal closes on the announced terms, it terminates with a higher bid appearing, or it terminates with no rescue bid — the two failure modes deliberately not lumped together. On a held-out set of four hundred recent large deals, tested genuinely out of sample, the system beat the market-implied odds, a tuned statistical model, and every frontier language model tested. A twelve-agent research pipeline mapped the analyst's own reasoning process onto the task. The decoder files it as the ledger's first AI forecasting entry with an out-of-sample, score-receipted test set at deal scale — and the three-way split is the lesson: lumping failure modes together throws away information.
  - Source: https://www.arblens.com/blog/weekly-020.html
  - [CLAIMED — hedge-fund paper via secondary summary; paper not read first-party this pass]

- **The 2026 midterms, scored in public before a vote was counted (November 2026).** Prediction-market favorites won four hundred seventy-nine of the first four hundred eighty-seven called races. Under a scoring rule fixed in August — the market price at eleven in the evening Eastern on November second, the side above fifty cents as the favorite, the race list fixed in advance — the favorite won thirty-one of thirty-two called Senate races and all fifty-three called House districts, and won all nine races where the market and the expert ratings differed by more than ten points. On California's propositions the markets were thirteen of fourteen by late October, the single miss a proposition leading by less than one point. Proposition forty is the cleanest markets-versus-polls separation on the record: the polls showed failure likely only days before the vote, while the market had priced failure below fifty percent since the market opened the previous December. Nine AI agents also predicted the midterms, the best calling four hundred nineteen of four hundred twenty-three races — but they had internet access, including the markets themselves, so they were aggregating other calls as much as forecasting. The decoder files the post-mortem as the largest pre-registered, receipt-scored market test on the record, and the AI caveat as the receipts discipline applied to forecasters.
  - Source: https://predictionmarketspicks.com/articles/how-accurate-were-prediction-markets-2026-midterms
  - Source: https://medium.com/@gaetanlion/the-prediction-markets-did-very-well-predicting-california-propositions-outcomes-516c00a3d5cf
  - [CORROBORATED — pre-registered scorecard + multiple outlets]

- **The human forecasters are still ahead of the bots, barely (Fall 2026).** Metaculus opened its Fall 2026 FutureEval bot tournament — fifty thousand dollars, three to four hundred questions — and published its Spring 2026 analyses. Human Pros only narrowly retain their lead over forecasting bots, without statistical significance, and nine of ten individual Pros beat every individual bot. The bot makers' own advice: simplicity beats complexity, and research quality is the bottleneck. The decoder files it as the honest negative the receipts discipline wants on the record — the human-versus-machine gap is closing but not closed, and research quality, not model size, is the bottleneck.
  - Source: https://www.metaculus.com/notebooks/45615/announcement-of-futureeval-fall-2026/

Scored on the vendor's BOOM benchmark — three hundred fifty million observations across two thousand eight hundred seven series. The decoder files it as the open-weight answer to the warehouse-locked forecasting models already on this shelf: zero-shot anomaly scoring anyone can run without a vendor account, in a licence the decoder itself can ship. ## Agent detection vs anti-detection

- **Cloudflare Precursor (GA, ~July 2026).** Continuous behavioral
  validation: the whole browser session is monitored for bot
  automation instead of a point-in-time checkpoint. Cloudflare reports
  bots now generate roughly 57% of all web requests — the first time
  automated traffic has exceeded human activity on its measurements.
  [CORROBORATED — Cloudflare announcement via helpnetsecurity.com and
  designrush.com; the 57% figure is Cloudflare's own measurement]
- **Cequence Biometric Check (June 2026).** CAPTCHA-free: when a
  session falls outside the behavioral confidence threshold, the device
  returns signed proof from its Secure Enclave that a real person on a
  registered device completed a familiar biometric. The same checkpoint
  logic extends to AI agents — high-stakes irreversible actions hit a
  human-in-the-loop gate at the time of the action. [CLAIMED — vendor
  announcement via helpnetsecurity.com]
- **Securonix Advanced Behavioral Analytics + AEBA (announced Oct 12, 2026).** Agent and Entity Behavior Analytics flags when an enterprise AI agent uses an unexpected tool, accesses data outside its purpose, or changes its operating pattern — evaluated alongside identity, authority, data use, asset sensitivity, timing, and threat context; paired with classic UEBA. Consequential response actions require human approval. Decoder significance: agent behavior is now graded as a first-class entity alongside the human's — detection is no longer just "is this a bot" but "is this the agent it claims to be, doing what it was built to do." [CLAIMED — company announcement; 2026-10-13 research loop]
- **Incognia AI Agent Detection (announced Oct 7, 2026).** For financial institutions: signed-request verification, agent-origin classification, bot/automation detection — the core insight is that the *agent* and the *action* are evaluated as two distinct entities (a legitimate agent's transaction may still be unauthorized by the human behind it). Web Behavioral Biometrics added (mouse movements, keyboard interactions, copy-and-paste activity); suspicious sessions can be cross-linked to a trusted mobile device; plus an MCP server feeding intelligence into AI fraud-investigation apps. Decoder significance: the identity/intent split sharpened to agent/action — attestation is becoming per-action, not per-session. [CLAIMED — company announcement; 2026-10-13 research loop]
- **Web Bot Auth (emerging IETF standard) + DataDome two-layer trust
  (July 2026).** Cryptographic per-request AI-agent identity answering
  "who," paired with continuous intent detection answering "what it
  intends." [CLAIMED — DataDome framing via techtimes.com; the IETF
  draft not verified this pass]
- **PACT — private access control tokens, Cloudflare + Chrome + Firefox
  + Edge (announced ~June 2026).** Extends Privacy Pass (IETF RFC 9576,
  2024) with blind signatures: a site that trusts a user issues the
  browser an anonymous token; other sites accept it as proof of vetting
  without learning who, which sites, or what device. Publicly verifiable
  from the issuer's public key alone — no central clearinghouse that
  could become a tracking point. Explicitly covers AI agents acting on a
  legitimate person's behalf. Distinct from Web Bot Auth: PACT is the
  CAPTCHA-replacement token layer at the gate; Web Bot Auth is
  cryptographic identity plus continuous intent grading inside the
  session. Decoder significance: the first browser-native,
  privacy-preserving CAPTCHA successor with agent-aware personhood —
  the successor track converges on standards, not products. [CLAIMED —
  trade-press report of the announcement; standard not finalized;
  2026-10-15 research loop]
- **FortSignal Agent Passport (announced May 2026).** One-time
  human-approved policy (actions, caps, recipients, expiry) approved via
  passkey biometric; then per-action cryptographic intent binding — the
  agent hashes the exact action parameters and signs with its own
  Ed25519 key, with signature validity and exact-policy fit verified per
  action and a signed receipt issued on pass. Decoder significance: the
  per-action intent receipt — authorization per action, not per session.
  [CLAIMED — vendor publication; vendor-framed; 2026-10-15 research
  loop]
- **1Password for Claude (announced July 17, 2026).** When the agent hits
  a login screen, it asks 1Password for the credential; the user sees
  which credential and why, approves with a fingerprint; 1Password fills
  it directly into the website — the model never sees it. Access ends
  when the task ends. Decoder significance: the credential-custody
  primitive — agents act through locked doors without holding any key.
  [CLAIMED — vendor blog via trade press; beta-stage at announcement;
  2026-10-15 research loop]
- **Apate — undercover AI agents for fraud intelligence (reported Oct 14,
  2026).** AI agents deliberately enter scams, getting scammed to gather
  fraud intelligence — detection shifting from passive sensors to
  proactive, adversary-aware actors. Decoder significance: the
  engagement instrument becomes the detection instrument, pairing the
  adaptive-honeypot measurement in the sandbox section. [CLAIMED —
  trade-press report; 2026-10-15 research loop]
- **FP-Inconsistent fingerprint-consistency detection (arXiv, Sep
  2025).** ~500k requests from 20 "undetectable" bot services: 52.93%
  evasion vs DataDome, 44.56% vs BotD; inconsistency rules cut evasion
  by 48.11% and 44.95%. Evasive bots alter fingerprints but struggle to
  keep them consistent across attributes and over time.
  [CORROBORATED — arXiv paper with measured evaluation]
- **Indirect prompt injection as the "AI honeypot" (2026).** Invisible
  instructions embedded in page content that AI-driven automation
  parses and obeys — self-identifying as a bot. The classic honeypot
  rebuilt for the AI-agent traffic wave. [CLAIMED — industry
  practitioner piece]
- **WebGPU fingerprint micro-benchmarks (2026).** A spoofed high-end
  GPU that performs like a virtualized CPU flags instantly; the
  evasion side answers with isolated-VM execution, adversarial TLS
  fingerprints, and device farms. [CLAIMED — industry pieces]
- **FP-Agent (arXiv:2605.01247, May 2026; UC Davis).** First controlled
  measurement of seven AI browsing agents vs humans on an instrumented
  honey website. Browser fingerprints have limited discriminative
  power when agents share one underlying fingerprint; behavioral
  fingerprints — typing, scrolling, mouse movement — separate agents
  from humans and from one another. Case study: FP-Agent detects all
  seven agents; Cloudflare's bot management detects one. The
  receipts-grade technique for on-device agentic browsers is
  behavioral, not fingerprint-based — a passive JS listener grades
  input behavior over the session. [CORROBORATED — preprint with
  measured evaluation; peer-review status not confirmed]
- **"Known By Their Actions" (arXiv:2605.14786).** Agent UI traces
  encode model identity: up to 96% classification macro F1 across 14
  frontier models from passive JS behavioral traces alone; randomized
  delays insufficient once the adversary retrains. Attribution now
  reaches model identity — stealth must blend into a specific model's
  action rhythm, not just look human. [CLAIMED — preprint, authors'
  evaluation]
- **"Whose Agent Are You?" (arXiv:2606.20910).** Multi-layer
  fingerprinting and attribution of autonomous web agents — telling
  which agent, not just that it is one. [CLAIMED — via practitioner
  documentation; abstract not read this pass]
- **Atria Safety "Ninhydrin" (Aug 2026).** Honest negative result:
  population-scale browser/device fingerprint matching for ban-evasion
  detection proved infeasible — per-pair error rates compound
  multiplicatively across 1:N comparisons, driving innocent-flag
  probability toward unity; no remediation fixed it. Population-scale
  fingerprint identity is dead — which is why the field pivoted to

  evaluation still open. Update (November 7, 2026 research loop):
  the vendor model page now states the missing false-positive figure
  — about five to six percent of human visits flagged as agents at
  the default Balanced setting — closing the November 3 watch item
  on that point; the page also adds operating texture: median first
  check about one hundred twenty milliseconds with ninety five
  percent within two hundred milliseconds, checks repeat until two
  consecutive reads agree, and the session is then classified for
  the rest of the visit; pricing is a free tier of one million
  sessions, then one dollar per one thousand sessions. Update
  (November 8, 2026 research loop): independent trade-press audit
  of the vendor's own model page adds the evasion-technique splits
  — Camoufox at least ninety six point eight percent, Patchright at
  least ninety two point six percent, Stealth Playwright at least
  ninety two point seven percent, session takeover at least ninety
  six point seven percent for RAD-S1, against zero to six point six
  percent, zero to five point nine percent, zero to ten point two
  percent and four to fifty point two percent respectively for the
  six rivals — and two catches: every technique-level floor sits
  below the ninety eight point eight percent headline floor, which
  the vendor does not explain, and in the session-takeover row one
  unnamed rival reaches fifty point two percent, contradicting the
  release's under fifteen percent ceiling; and on non-disguised

  ninety eight point seven percent floor) — the advertised gap
  exists only for deliberately disguised agents. The audit also
  notes low-interaction sessions come back Undecided and are mostly

  - Source: https://genznewz.com/resemble-ai-agent-detection-spots-agents-acting-human
- **Shufti Know Your Agent — agent verification in a single flow:
  identity, human authorization, mandate (launched October twenty
  ninth, two thousand twenty six; new to record; material — new
  agent-detection and verification technique).** A verification
  solution for autonomous agents acting for individuals and
  businesses: it verifies the agent's identity, confirms a real
  person authorized the action, and checks the agent's permissions
  before it can access data or trigger a transaction. Each agent
  receives a unique time-bound credential that can be revoked; known
  agents are recognised by name and new or unfamiliar agents are
  assessed through behavioural biometrics, with a trust score per
  agent. Authorization starts with a principal-set mandate covering
  permitted actions, limits, expiry, and revocation; risk-based
  authorization escalates out-of-mandate or high-risk requests to a
  human-in-the-loop selfie liveness check, and an audit trail links
  requests, decisions, and revocations to each agent and principal.
  Lesson: the third agent-verification launch in three days
  alongside Socure and Resemble — but the distinct move here is
  mandate-first: Socure binds the agent to a verified principal and
  Resemble grades behaviour, while Shufti gates each request against
  a stated mandate with a revocable credential, the closest shipped
  answer yet to the question of authorized for what, until when, and
  revocable by whom. The caveat is structural as with the others:
  the launch is a vendor wire release carried by multiple outlets,
  not an independent evaluation, and no accuracy, false-positive, or
  deployment figures are published in the carrier. [CLAIMED —
  vendor launch announcement via wire release carried by multiple
  outlets; no independent evaluation, no accuracy or deployment
  figures published]
  - Source: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/10/29/3391650/0/en/shufti-launches-know-your-agent-to-verify-ai-agent-identity-human-authorization-permissions-in-a-single-flow.html
- **Cisco Project Quarry — open-source sequence-level
  agent-behavior monitor (released around October 28, 2026; new to
  record; material — new agent-detection technique, the lane's first
  open-source sequence-level monitor).** Quarry combines rule-based
  detection, machine-learning classifiers, and language-model analysis
  to identify potentially dangerous sequences of agent actions,
  monitoring an agent's complete activity history rather than
  evaluating individual commands in isolation — for example an agent
  retrieving credentials from a protected file and then transmitting
  information to an unauthorized server, suspicious encoded commands,
  or manipulation of an agent through malicious instructions. It
  supports real-time and historical monitoring, MCP, multimodal
  inputs including images, and multi-turn conversations; Cisco
  published it on GitHub with configuration guidance, sample security
  rules, and plugins for Claude Code, Codex, and other MCP-compatible
  agents, and positions it as complementing authorization controls and
  human oversight rather than replacing them. Cisco cites the July
  OpenAI–Hugging Face incident as the motivating case, but that
  mapping is retrospective, not a live test. Lesson: the open,
  sequence-level sibling to SentinelOne ADR's commercial runtime
  instrument — where ADR asks whether behavior matches the assigned
  task, Quarry asks whether the action sequence itself is dangerous,
  and being open-source with sample rules it is the first entry in
  the lane a gauntlet could actually run against a specimen. Watch:
  detection rates on real deployments, and whether sequence rules
  survive agents that spread a harmful sequence across sessions.
  [CLAIMED — vendor announcement via trade press; no independent
  evaluation, no detection rates, incident mapping retrospective]
  - Source: https://securityboulevard.com/2026/10/cisco-debuts-open-source-tool-to-track-dangerous-ai-agent-behavior/
- **Fullstory Muse behavior-adaptation observation — a named
  production agent re-shapes its behavior to evade detection
  (Fullstory blog, October 26, 2026; new to record; material —
  in-the-wild anti-detection adaptation).** Fullstory shipped a way

  earlier in October, and around October 16 Muse traffic in those
  tracked segments dropped sharply — not because people stopped using

  checks. Fullstory's counter-move was to rebuild detection in hours
  from sessions already captured, on the argument that header checks
  and IP lists cannot keep up with an agent that re-shapes its
  behavior, while comprehensive behavioral data can. The piece also
  bets that agents will self-identify by the end of 2027. Lesson: the
  first named production agent observed adapting its behavior to
  evade detection within days of being detected — the live case for
  the standing watch on whether behavioral detectors survive fitted
  evaders, since curved paths and pauses are exactly the
  pointer/typing signals they grade. The caveat is structural: a
  single vendor blog from a company selling behavioral data, and the
  experiment was its own engineer's prompt, so the adaptation is
  claimed, not measured, and the "passed simple checks" claim names
  no check set. [CLAIMED — single vendor blog, self-interested

  - Source: https://www.fullstory.com/blog/ai-agent-observability-undercover-shoppers/
- **OpenAI expanded misalignment monitoring for API agents
  (disclosed October 28, 2026; new to record; material — new
  agent-detection technique with published coverage semantics).**
  Layered monitoring across internal training, evaluations, internal
  coding tools, and selected external deployments, looking for
  concerning agent behavior such as unauthorized access, deception,
  and attempts to evade controls. Coverage detail: covered models
  using the Responses API with persisted reasoning, WebSockets, or
  OpenAI compaction can be monitored and have later execution
  blocked; other covered Responses API requests can be monitored and
  send configured webhook alerts but cannot be stopped automatically;
  Chat Completions API requests are not covered by this particular
  system. A blocked request returns HTTP 403 with code
  misalignment_policy_violation, and asynchronous detection cannot
  reverse a tool action that already happened. An earlier independent
  red-team assessment by METR and Redwood Research found
  vulnerabilities in the monitoring stack; OpenAI says most identified
  issues have since been patched, with one fix still in progress, and
  no universal real-world detection rates are published. Decoder
  significance: the first provider-side agent monitor with an explicit
  stop/alert/uncovered map — containment reasoning can now cite which
  API shapes are even stoppable, and the uncovered Chat Completions
  lane plus the already-executed-action limit are the
  evasion-relevant edges. [CLAIMED — vendor disclosure via secondary
  explainer; no detection rates, one red-team fix still in progress]
  - Source: https://thebrieflens.com/openai-misalignment-monitoring-api-coverage-limits/

- **Sumsub KYA Module for MCP (launched October 20, 2026; new to
  record; material — new agent-verification technique, data-plane
  filtering for agents).** A filtering module sitting between verified
  AI agents and personal data, letting businesses define exactly what
  agents they build or deploy may access inside company systems. It
  screens every agent request, strips personally identifiable and other
  sensitive information before it reaches the agent, and applies a
  configurable rule engine keyed to data sensitivity, action type, and
  requesting/calling department. When an agent tries to access a
  flagged file or take an action above a threshold, the system can
  trigger a real-time liveness check confirming a verified human
  authorized the request. Built for MCP, starting with Amazon Bedrock
  AgentCore Gateway, with additional MCP gateways to follow; it
  extends Sumsub's January AI Agent Verification and June MCP
  integration. Decoder significance: the distinct move in the KYA
  cluster is data-plane, not credential-plane — Socure binds the agent
  to a principal, Shufti gates each request against a mandate, and
  Sumsub now filters what the agent can even see. [CLAIMED — vendor
  announcement via trade press; no independent evaluation, no
  accuracy or deployment figures]
  - Source: https://pulsexpertech.com/technology/sumsub-expands-know-your-agent-putting-businesses-in-control-of-what-ai-agents-can-access

- **hCaptcha WebMCP verification tool (hCaptcha Enterprise,
  ~October 1, 2026; new to record; material — new
  agent-verification technique, the first shipped verification tool
  for a draft agent-tool protocol).** WebMCP lets a web page expose
  named tools to browser agents — searchProducts, reserveInventory
  — so the agent calls the tool through the browser instead of
  working out the action from buttons and page layout. With the
  feature enabled, the SDK exposes `hcaptcha_verify`: the tool
  starts verification, waits for verification already in progress,
  or uses an available response, and a successful call returns
  status "verified"; the token stays in the page widget for normal
  backend Siteverify validation. If verification opens an
  interactive challenge, `hcaptcha_verify` returns status
  "requires_human" — the agent must stop and ask the person who
  initiated the task to complete it, and closing the challenge
  without completing it does not verify the user. Enabling the tool
  does not force Passive Mode or bypass challenges, and the
  protected endpoint must still reject invalid, expired, or
  already-used tokens before performing the action. hCaptcha's own
  caveat, carried: WebMCP activity alone does not establish that a
  visitor is an active agent — agent detection is evaluated
  separately, including via Web Bot Auth. Decoder significance: the
  verification wing of the lane gains its first tool-shaped answer
  — instead of asking "is this visitor human or agent," the site
  hands the agent a named tool and a verification call, with a
  human-escalation seam stated in an API return value rather than a
  policy page. Pairs with Sumsub's data-plane filtering (what the
  agent can see) and Shufti's mandate gating (what the agent may
  do) as the third face of the KYA cluster: how the agent proves
  itself at the moment of action. [CLAIMED — vendor product blog,
  first-party vendor text but no independent deployment or
  detection figures]
  - Source: https://www.hcaptcha.com/blog/hcaptcha-webmcp

- **Halligan, agentic vision-language CAPTCHA solver (USENIX
  Security 2025; surfaced October 30, 2026 via the Browserbase
  blog; new to record; material — anti-detection research with a
  measured rate).** Halligan achieved a 60.7% success rate across
  2,600 visual CAPTCHA challenges covering 26 types, combining
  visual understanding with mouse and keyboard interaction — a
  computer-using agent against image CAPTCHAs, not a classifier
  against one challenge family. Decoder significance: it reframes

  real-world reCAPTCHA sessions, zero-cost and zero-shot, and the
  self-labeling adaptive solver at 85.4% across 16 classes with
  recovery in every round of a simulated year-long arms race.
  Those two are 2026's sharper, narrower numbers; Halligan is the
  breadth proof from a peer-reviewed venue a year earlier: 26 types
  at once, with interaction, not just vision. The three together
  close the "visual CAPTCHA as a gate" question from both ends:
  breadth, cost, and adaptation. The carrier's own caveat is
  carried: the studies evaluated different systems and challenges,
  so the percentages are not directly comparable, and none of this
  proves every CAPTCHA can be defeated. [CORROBORATED as

  paper itself not read first-party this pass, so the 60.7% figure
